title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live iOS Apps
excerpt: While frontier vision-language models demonstrate strong capabilities in user interface (UI) navigation, their high inference costs prohibit everyday use. Conversely, smaller models trained via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or offline reinforcement learning often memorize static trajectories, leading to brittle execution and an inability to recover from errors. To address these limitations, we propose a novel online reinforcement learning framework that trains UI navigation agents directly on live iOS applications. Our framework decouples the agent into two specialized components: a Planning…

ai.summary: Apple Machine Learning proposes an online dense reinforcement learning framework for UI navigation agents that trains directly on live iOS apps, overcoming the brittleness of static supervised fine-tuning and the high cost of frontier VLMs.
ai.why: Provides a method for building robust, low-cost mobile UI automation agents that can adapt to dynamic app states in real-time.

title: ReLift: Dense 3D Tracking as Lifted Trajectory Repair
excerpt: Dense 3D tracking from monocular video requires establishing point correspondences over time, estimating their depth, and inferring their trajectories during occlusion. Existing methods typically learn these tasks jointly, a demanding objective given the scarcity of 4D supervision. We show that strong pretrained 2D trackers and 3D geometry models provide an effective foundation: lifted trajectories, with occluded segments simply interpolated, already rival dedicated 3D trackers using the same geometry. However, lifted trajectories inherit correspondence and depth errors, and under occlusion, their depth comes from the occluder rather than the tracked point. We introduce ReLift, an efficient…

ai.summary: The paper proposes ReLift, a method that uses pretrained 2D trackers and 3D geometry models to lift monocular video points into dense 3D trajectories, interpolating occluded segments, achieving performance comparable to dedicated 3D trackers.
ai.why: It shows developers can leverage existing 2D tracking models for 3D tasks without heavy 4D supervision, simplifying pipeline construction.

title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
excerpt: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control. However, they still require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, incurring substantial latency and hindering real-time deployment. Simply reducing the number of denoising steps will collapse the nonlinear multi-step denoising trajectory into coarse updates, substantially degrading action quality. To reduce the denoising steps while enabling real-time action generation, we present an effective world action model with one-step action generation, namely OSWAM…

ai.summary: OSWAM introduces a one‑step action generation method for World Action Models, reducing denoising steps while maintaining action quality for autonomous driving and embodied control.
ai.why: It enables lower‑latency inference for real‑time control systems, useful for developers building autonomous agents.

title: Venus-DefakerOne2: A Vision-Forensics Foundation Model with Broader Coverage
excerpt: Real-world forgery is inherently heterogeneous: it manifests not only as digital manipulation but also as physical spoofing, and is carried not only by images but also by videos. Despite substantial progress, a unified anti-forgery foundation model covering such a broad threat spectrum remains absent. In this paper, we present Venus-DefakerOne2, which substantially extends the forensic capability boundary along both the forgery-form and media-type dimensions. Trained on tens of millions of open-source and in-house samples, it incorporates two key designs. Tide-Style-Tuning alternates LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning to balance computational efficiency, generalization, and hard-sample…

ai.summary: The paper introduces Venus-DefakerOne2, a vision‑forensics foundation model trained on tens of millions of samples to detect both digital and physical forgeries across images and videos.
ai.why: Provides a more comprehensive anti‑forgery tool that developers can integrate into content‑verification pipelines.

title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
excerpt: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) achieve remarkable success on diverse multimodal understanding and generation tasks, yet they still struggle to effectively leverage language-based chain-of-thought reasoning for image generation. As a result, existing reasoning-augmented UMMs often fail to inherit the test-time scaling and fine-grained controllability observed in large language models. We attribute this failure to a fundamental modality mismatch: reasoning is performed in a discrete token space, whereas image generation operates in a continuous space. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Latent Reasoning framework in Continuous space (LARC), which alleviates the token-level bottleneck by…

ai.summary: The paper proposes a latent‑space reasoning approach for Unified Multimodal Models to enable chain‑of‑thought style reasoning for image generation, addressing the token‑space mismatch of prior methods.
ai.why: Could improve multimodal generation tools developers use, making them more controllable and scalable.

title: GLOW-FM: Efficient Generative Low-Light Image Enhancement with One-Step Latent Flow Matching
excerpt: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) aims to recover well-exposed and perceptually faithful images from severely degraded observations. Recent diffusion-based generative methods achieve strong perceptual quality by leveraging powerful image priors, but their iterative sampling incurs substantial computational cost, limiting practical deployment. Despite recent efficiency gains in generative LLIE, high-quality enhancement with a single function evaluation and low overall computation remains challenging, particularly under diverse real-world low-light conditions. We introduce GLOW-FM, a one-step latent flow-matching framework for efficient generative LLIE. GLOW-FM performs conditional transport…

ai.summary: GLOW-FM is a generative model for low-light image enhancement that uses one-step latent flow matching to achieve high-quality results with significantly lower computational cost than iterative diffusion methods.

title: Wizard: Manipulate Any World in Real Time via Agentic Control
excerpt: Recent advances in video world models have enabled the generation of increasingly realistic and interactive virtual environments, opening new possibilities for player-customizable gameplay. Agentic frameworks further advance this direction by decoupling explicit game logic and controllable world representations from visual generation. However, existing approaches support only simple game settings and predefined motion patterns, generalize poorly to unseen environments and characters, and offer limited real-time interactivity. In this paper, we introduce Wizard, an agentic game world model that enables real-time, precise control over character motions while generalizing zero-shot across…

ai.summary: Wizard enables real‑time manipulation of any virtual world by decoupling explicit game logic from visual generation, allowing agents to control environments beyond predefined settings.

title: CEPO: A General Framework for Improving Prompt Optimization in Multi-Agent Systems
excerpt: Multi-agent systems (MAS) require both effective coordination and specialized task execution. Existing prompt optimization approaches typically couple these functions within agent-specific prompts. We introduce Coordinator-Executor Prompt Optimization (CEPO), a general framework for improving prompt optimization in MAS. CEPO separates system-level coordination from agent-level execution through a shared coordinator prompt and agent-specific executor prompts, and guides their updates according to their respective roles. This structure allows shared coordination rules to be refined consistently across agents while keeping execution instructions separately adjustable. CEPO provides the prompt…

ai.summary: CEPO (Coordinator‑Executor Prompt Optimization) separates system‑level coordination prompts from agent‑level execution prompts and updates them jointly to improve multi‑agent prompt performance.
ai.why: Offers a practical framework for refining prompts in complex multi‑agent deployments.

title: WeFair: Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in Short-Video Search
excerpt: Short-video search needs compact query rewriters that recover users' personalized intent from ambiguous queries under strict latency constraints. Existing LLM-based methods have improved rewriting by using synthetic reasoning and subsequent consumption-behavioral feedback. However, overemphasizing subsequent consumption can favor engaging content over the user's immediate need, causing intent drift even when rewritten queries are grounded in behavioral history. We propose WeFair, Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in WeChat short-video search. WeFair uses human feedback according to how directly it reflects personalized intent, assigning feedback…

ai.summary: WeFair proposes a fidelity‑aware alignment method that rewrites short‑video search queries using human feedback while preserving user intent and meeting strict latency constraints.

title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
excerpt: Across coding, web, and tool-use tasks, language-model agents are now routinely trained with the same recipe: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to learn the interface, then multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) to master it. Code-as-policy (CaP) casts robot manipulation in the same form, as the policy writes code against robot APIs and reads back the results, so the same recipe should apply. Yet existing CaP agents sidestep training: they either prompt closed frontier models or delegate manipulation to pre-trained vision-language-action models (VLAs) and high-level skills, while small open vision-language models (VLMs) fail outright. We present CaPtain, an open post-training pipeline that turns…

ai.summary: CaPtain introduces a pipeline that applies supervised fine‑tuning and multi‑turn reinforcement learning to train code‑as‑policy robot agents, enabling them to generate and execute robot API code.
ai.why: Gives developers a concrete training recipe for building robot agents that write and run their own control code.

title: Does Scaling Toward AGI Depend on What System-1 Lets System-2 Execute?
excerpt: Progress toward artificial general intelligence (AGI) has largely relied on scaling a resource-intensive executive, System-2, through larger models, more data and compute, longer reasoning, and more agents. We ask whether the next stage may come instead from co-designing it with System-1, a lightweight, semantically aware predictor that evaluates candidate interactions before execution, so that System-2 acts only on those worth their cost. Our answer is a qualified yes. We study conditional interaction, a predict--gate--execute--update loop: System-1 estimates each candidate's utility, System-2 executes those admitted by an adaptive threshold, and the outcomes update System-1. The loop…

ai.summary: Researchers propose co‑designing a lightweight System‑1 predictor with the resource‑heavy System‑2 executor, showing that conditional evaluation of actions can reduce compute while preserving performance.
ai.why: Suggests a more efficient scaling path toward AGI that developers can explore by integrating fast predictors into existing pipelines.

title: FrameForge: Harnessing Priors of Video Foundation Models for Unified Image Generation
excerpt: Unified conditional image generation requires a single model to preserve different aspects of a visual input while producing a target image that follows textual guidance. Pretrained video models provide a promising foundation by encoding visual transformations across time, yet existing approaches typically assign the condition and target to fixed temporal positions. We observe that condition-target relationships vary substantially across generation tasks, while video models naturally encode visual transformations at different temporal scales. This motivates us to model conditional generation through input-adaptive virtual temporal relations. We propose FrameForge, which captures two…

ai.summary: FrameForge leverages priors from pretrained video foundation models to build a unified image generation system that flexibly handles varying condition‑target relationships across tasks.
ai.why: Provides a method to reuse temporal video knowledge for more versatile image synthesis.

title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
excerpt: A capable voice assistant must do more than recognize words; it must understand requests, reason over context, sustain conversations, and act through tools. We present Apriel Voice 27B Preview, an open speech-language model that unifies these capabilities within a shared reasoning backbone while retaining text and image input modalities. Built on the post-trained Gemma 4 26B-A4B checkpoint, Apriel Voice directly processes speech and generates both responses and tool calls without requiring a separate dialogue model. We introduce a two-stage training procedure to adapt the model to speech. The first stage establishes the speech interface, while the second jointly adapts the projector and…

title: HiFOR: Hierarchical Foresight with Action-Guided World Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Model
excerpt: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated promising capabilities in robotic manipulation by integrating visual perception, language understanding, and action generation. Recent advances have further incorporated future prediction to enhance the understanding of environmental dynamics and task progression. However, existing methods often model short-term dynamics and long-term task objectives separately, while directly incorporating predicted futures into action policies without sufficiently considering their relevance to current action requirements. To address these limitations, we propose HiFOR, a hierarchical foresight framework with action-guided world retrieval…

ai.summary: HiFOR presents a hierarchical foresight model that grounds actions in predicted future world states, integrating long‑term dynamics into vision‑language‑action policies for robotic manipulation.

title: R^2Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
excerpt: In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R^2Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for…

title: REA: A Routed Embodied Agent Runtime for Asynchronous Brain-Cerebellum Control
excerpt: Foundation models are becoming remarkably reliable at high-level reasoning, yet they remain too slow and costly to serve as fine-grained controllers. Conversely, fast policies like VLAs and whole-body controllers offer more efficient reflexes, but struggle to generalize. While pairing a deliberative brain (foundation models) with a reactive cerebellum (fast policies) seems natural for embodied systems, two obstacles remain: methods are built and scored on incompatible stacks, and their asynchronous coordination is difficult. For example, an agent that calls the VLA in the agentic loop can stall the fast execution, while a VLA that calls the agent on errors tends to re-trigger fallbacks…

ai.summary: The paper introduces REA, a runtime that pairs slow foundation models for high-level reasoning with fast policies for reactive control in embodied agents, addressing latency and generalization gaps in current brain-cerebellum architectures.
ai.why: Offers a concrete architectural pattern for developers building real-time robotic or embodied AI systems that need both strategic planning and fast reflexes.

title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
excerpt: Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) on instruction data can quietly erode their safety, even when no training example looks harmful. By simplifying a low-rank attribution method and restricting backpropagation to the final four transformer blocks, SimpleLoRIF can embed datasets on the order of a million examples, boosting gradient attribution from a small-scale analysis tool into a practical filter for full post-training…

title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
excerpt: An observer sees only part of the surrounding world, yet must keep track of what lies beyond the current view. Spatial perception therefore involves more than recognizing individual images: it calls for a persistent spatial state that is updated under self-motion and used to guide action. Do visual foundation models provide representations that support such a state? We study this question through four levels of spatial capability---spatial structure, object persistence, predictive spatial update, and actionability---using frozen-feature probes on ten representations under streaming egocentric observations of static indoor environments. The resulting capability profiles vary across tasks…

ai.summary: The paper investigates whether visual foundation models encode persistent spatial state by evaluating them on four capabilities: spatial structure, object persistence, predictive spatial update, and action guidance.
ai.why: Results inform developers about the suitability of existing vision models for tasks requiring ongoing spatial awareness, such as robotics or AR.

title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
excerpt: Achieving the broad task generalization of embodied models in physical environments remains a central challenge in robot learning. We study this challenge in World Action Models (WAMs) through two complementary capabilities: video generalization, which predicts the visual evolution of new tasks, and action generalization, which translates these predictions into executable behavior through a video-to-action bridge. By varying video and action supervision for tasks outside an initial training set, we examine their respective contributions to task transfer. On RoboTwin 2.0, using only in-distribution video-action supervision yields a 25.07% success rate on out-of-distribution tasks…

ai.summary: WorldBridge proposes a video‑to‑action bridge that connects video prediction (video generalization) with executable behavior (action generalization) to improve task generalisation in World Action Models for embodied robotics.
